narrative.intro: OptumServe Health Services has $1.9B in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. OptumServe Health Services won 14 awards this fiscal year so far, with an average award size of $137M and obligations down 24.5% year over year. OptumServe Health Services received the bulk of FY2026 obligations from the Department of Veterans Affairs, which obligated $1.9B. OptumServe Health Services sells primarily physician and outpatient care services, with Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists) accounting for $1.9B of obligations in FY2026 to date. OptumServe Health Services recorded multi-year growth and fluctuation in prior years: FY21 obligations were $756M, FY22 obligations were $874M, FY23 obligations were $711M, FY24 obligations were $1.6B, and FY25 obligations were $2.5B. OptumServe Health Services also has smaller FY2026 obligations from the Department of Defense and the Department of Health and Human Services, recorded at $16.3M and $11.5M respectively. OptumServe Health Services participates in several outpatient NAICS markets including Offices of Physicians, Mental Health Specialists at $11M and All Other Outpatient Care Centers at $10.8M.

sections.heading: How have OptumServe Health Services obligations changed over recent fiscal years?
sections.body: OptumServe Health Services obligations rose and fell across FY21 to FY25 before settling at $1.9B in FY26 to date. OptumServe Health Services recorded FY21 obligations of $756M, FY22 obligations of $874M, FY23 obligations of $711M, FY24 obligations of $1.6B, and FY25 obligations of $2.5B. OptumServe Health Services obligations in FY2026 to date are down 24.5% year over year. OptumServe Health Services has an average award size of $137M for the 14 awards received so far this fiscal year.

sections.heading: Who are the main federal buyers and what markets does OptumServe Health Services serve?
sections.body: OptumServe Health Services receives the largest FY2026 obligations from the Department of Veterans Affairs, which obligated $1.9B. OptumServe Health Services also has FY2026 obligations from the Department of Defense at $16.3M and the Department of Health and Human Services at $11.5M. OptumServe Health Services serves primarily physician and outpatient markets, with Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists) at $1.9B, Offices of Physicians, Mental Health Specialists at $11M, and All Other Outpatient Care Centers at $10.8M. OptumServe Health Services also records obligations in All Other Miscellaneous Ambulatory Health Care Services at $719K.

faq.q: How much does OptumServe Health Services make from federal contracts?
faq.a: OptumServe Health Services has $1.9B in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. OptumServe Health Services won 14 awards so far this fiscal year, with an average award size of $137M. OptumServe Health Services obligations are down 24.5% year over year.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from OptumServe Health Services?
faq.a: The Department of Veterans Affairs is the largest buyer of OptumServe Health Services in FY2026 to date, obligating $1.9B. The Department of Defense bought from OptumServe Health Services for $16.3M and the Department of Health and Human Services bought from OptumServe Health Services for $11.5M.

faq.q: What does OptumServe Health Services sell to the government?
faq.a: OptumServe Health Services sells physician and ambulatory health services to the federal government. OptumServe Health Services sells through Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists) at $1.9B, Offices of Physicians, Mental Health Specialists at $11M, All Other Outpatient Care Centers at $10.8M, and All Other Miscellaneous Ambulatory Health Care Services at $719K in FY2026 to date.
